title: Serotonin receptor type 7 (5-HT7) promotes colorectal cancer progression by activating Wnt/beta-catenin signaling via interacting with CK1epsilon.
authors: Lv, Moyang; Hu, Changjiang; Li, Jie; Zhang, Yuchen; Lu, Cheng; Zhang, Shengwei; He, Lijiao; Li, Hongwei; Ouyang, Qin; Yang, Shiming
one_liner_zh: 该文研究5-HT7受体与CK1epsilon蛋白互作激活Wnt信号促进结直肠癌，虽含分子对接但对象为蛋白-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT; serotonin), a well-known neurotransmitter, can promote the development of colorectal cancer (CRC). 5-HT exerts distinct physiological and pathological effects through engagement with specific 5-HT receptors. However, the receptors mediating tumor-promoting effects in CRC remain largely unknown. Here, we found that 5-HT receptor 7 (5-HT7) was significantly upregulated in CRC tumor tissues. Elevated 5-HT7 protein levels correlated positively with tumor burden, pathological grade, and lymph node metastasis, and negatively with overall survival in CRC patients. In CRC cells, lentivirus-mediated 5-HT7 overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas RNA interference-mediated knockdown suppressed these processes. 5-HT (10 muM) increased 5-HT7 expression and had similar tumor-promoting effects in CRC cells, which were suppressed by 5-HT7 knockdown. In nude mice, 5-HT7 overexpression increased tumor size and lung metastasis, while knockdown produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, 5-HT7 interacted with CK1epsilon, leading to Dishevelled (Dvl) phosphorylation, beta-catenin accumulation, and activation of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. CK1epsilon knockdown or treatment with the CK1epsilon-specific inhibitor PF4800567 blocked 5-HT7-induced Wnt/beta-catenin activation and reduced tumor growth and metastasis. Molecular docking and mutagenesis assays identified R13 and R372 in CK1epsilon and R427 and W472 in 5-HT7 as key residues mediating their interaction. These sites were essential for 5-HT7-driven Wnt/beta-catenin activation. Collectively, this study identifies 5-HT7 as a functional receptor promoting CRC progression via Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. These findings support the therapeutic potential of targeting 5-HT7 and its interaction with CK1epsilon in CRC.
abstract_zh: 5-羟色胺（5-HT；血清素）是一种众所周知的神经递质，可促进结直肠癌（CRC）的发展。5-HT通过与特定的5-HT受体结合发挥不同的生理和病理效应。然而，在CRC中介导促肿瘤效应的受体在很大程度上仍不明确。在此，我们发现5-HT受体7（5-HT7）在CRC肿瘤组织中显著上调。5-HT7蛋白水平升高与CRC患者的肿瘤负荷、病理分级和淋巴结转移呈正相关，与总生存期呈负相关。在CRC细胞中，慢病毒介导的5-HT7过表达增强了增殖、迁移和侵袭能力，而RNA干扰介导的敲低则抑制了这些过程。5-HT（10 μM）增加了5-HT7表达，并在CRC细胞中产生类似的促肿瘤效应，这些效应被5-HT7敲低所抑制。在裸鼠中，5-HT7过表达增加了肿瘤大小和肺转移，而敲低则产生相反的效果。机制上，5-HT7与CK1ε相互作用，导致Dishevelled（Dvl）磷酸化、β-catenin积累以及Wnt/β-catenin信号通路的激活。CK1ε敲低或使用CK1ε特异性抑制剂PF4800567处理可阻断5-HT7诱导的Wnt/β-catenin激活，并减少肿瘤生长和转移。分子对接和突变分析确定了CK1ε中的R13和R372以及5-HT7中的R427和W472是介导其相互作用的关键残基。这些位点对于5-HT7驱动的Wnt/β-catenin激活至关重要。总体而言，本研究将5-HT7确定为通过Wnt/β-catenin信号促进CRC进展的功能性受体。这些发现支持靶向5-HT7及其与CK1ε相互作用在CRC中的治疗潜力。
